response.sql:
WITH client_counts_by_district AS (
  SELECT 
    d.A3 as region,
    c.district_id,
    COUNT(*) as num_clients
  FROM client c
  JOIN district d ON c.district_id = d.district_id
  GROUP BY d.A3, c.district_id
),
region_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    region,
    num_clients,
    SUM(num_clients) OVER (PARTITION BY region) as total_clients_in_region
  FROM client_counts_by_district
)
SELECT 
  region,
  AVG(CAST(num_clients AS REAL)) as avg_clients_per_district,
  AVG(CAST(num_clients AS REAL) / total_clients_in_region) as avg_share
FROM region_stats
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY region;

assumptions.assumption: "The location of their branch" refers to client.district_id (the district directly associated with each client), not the account's branch district. This is the most direct reading, since the request says "their branch" (referring to clients), not "their account's branch."

alternatives.interpretation: If "their branch" should refer to account branches instead, you would join through the disp table to account.district_id. This counts clients per account district, deduplicating if a client has multiple accounts in the same district.
alternatives.sql:
WITH client_account_district AS (
  SELECT 
    DISTINCT c.client_id,
    a.district_id,
    d.A3 as region
  FROM client c
  JOIN disp dp ON c.client_id = dp.client_id
  JOIN account a ON dp.account_id = a.account_id
  JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
),
client_counts_by_district AS (
  SELECT 
    region,
    district_id,
    COUNT(*) as num_clients
  FROM client_account_district
  GROUP BY region, district_id
),
region_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    region,
    num_clients,
    SUM(num_clients) OVER (PARTITION BY region) as total_clients_in_region
  FROM client_counts_by_district
)
SELECT 
  region,
  AVG(CAST(num_clients AS REAL)) as avg_clients_per_district,
  AVG(CAST(num_clients AS REAL) / total_clients_in_region) as avg_share
FROM region_stats
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY region;
